faqs.question: What is the difference between a website and a web application?
faqs.answer: A website primarily presents content, while a web application lets users perform tasks, manage data or complete workflows. Many modern platforms combine both: public, SEO-friendly pages on the front and authenticated application functionality behind them.

faqs.question: How much does web development cost?
faqs.answer: Web development cost depends on scope, integrations, migration, performance requirements and compliance. A focused website or portal costs materially less than an integration-heavy enterprise web application. A useful estimate should show the assumptions and workstreams driving the range.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build a web application?
faqs.answer: A focused first release may take around three to five months, while a broader custom web application with complex integrations can take five to nine months or longer. Final timing depends on scope, dependencies and the level of testing required.

faqs.question: How do you make a website pass Core Web Vitals?
faqs.answer: Start with the rendering strategy, image delivery, JavaScript weight, fonts, caching and third-party scripts. We set performance budgets during development and use Lighthouse or equivalent checks in CI so regressions are caught before release.

faqs.question: How do you avoid losing SEO traffic during a website migration?
faqs.answer: Preserve valuable URLs where possible, map every changed URL to the correct redirect, carry over metadata and structured data, maintain canonicals, validate internal links and submit updated sitemaps. Crawl the old and new sites before cutover so missing or incorrect redirects are found early.

faqs.question: WordPress vs headless CMS vs custom build: which should we choose?
faqs.answer: Choose WordPress when standard content publishing covers most requirements, a headless CMS when editors need structured content across multiple channels, and custom web development when workflows, integrations or application logic are the differentiator. The right choice depends on operating needs, not trend.

faqs.question: Who owns the code and hosting after launch?
faqs.answer: Ownership is explicit in the agreement. AptenTech engagements define repository access, infrastructure, design files, documentation and handover terms from the start, so you are not dependent on the web development company after launch.
